title: Distance Between Bus Stops
statement:
A circular bus route has `n` stops labelled `0` to `n - 1`. The road from stop `i` to stop `(i + 1) % n` has length `distance[i]`, so the last stop connects back to stop `0`. Buses run both ways around the circle.

Return the length of the shorter way around from stop `start` to stop `destination` (this is `0` when the two stops are the same).
signature: int distanceBetweenBusStops(int[] distance, int start, int destination)
notes:
## Intuition

On a circle there are only two ways from one stop to another: one way covers the roads between the two stops in increasing index order, and the other way covers every remaining road. So if the first way has length `clockwise` and all roads add up to `total`, the other way is `total - clockwise`. Simulating both rides around the circle also works, but one pass with a little arithmetic is simpler.

## Approach

1. Let `from` be the smaller of `start` and `destination`, and `to` the larger, so the direction no longer matters.
2. Walk over every road `i`, adding `distance[i]` to `total`.
3. If `from <= i < to`, that road lies between the two stops on the increasing side, so add it to `clockwise` too.
4. Return the smaller of `clockwise` and `total - clockwise`.

## Example 1, step by step

`distance = [1, 2, 3, 4]`, `start = 0`, `destination = 1`, so `from = 0` and `to = 1`. Only road `0` is between them, so `clockwise = 1`. All roads give `total = 10`, and the other way is `10 - 1 = 9`. The answer is `min(1, 9) = 1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over `distance`.
- Space: O(1): only a few counters.

## Pitfalls

- `start` may be greater than `destination`; swapping them into `from` and `to` keeps the range test simple and gives the same pair of distances.
- Road `i` joins stops `i` and `i + 1`, so the range is `from <= i < to`, not `<= to`.
- When `start === destination` the range is empty and the answer is `0`, not the full loop.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `from`, `to` | the smaller and larger stop index |
| `total` | length of the whole loop |
| `clockwise` | length of the roads from `from` up to `to` |
| `i` | index of the current road |

narration.2: Take the smaller stop index as from, so the direction of the trip does not matter.
narration.3: And the larger stop index as to.
narration.4: total will be the length of the whole loop.
narration.5: clockwise will be the length of the roads between from and to on the increasing side.
narration.8: Every road belongs to the full loop.
narration.9: Road i joins stops i and i + 1, so it lies between from and to exactly when from <= i < to.
narration.10: Add it to the increasing-side length.
narration.13: The other way round uses all remaining roads; return the shorter of the two.
